You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Korean Media Rumors Crash Storage Sector? Google Added to Dow Jones; Micron Earnings Coming Up

TEXT:
I. Hot News
Federal Reserve Developments US June PMI Preliminary Beats Expectations, Employment Indicators Weak
Composite PMI preliminary rose to 52.2, Manufacturing PMI reached 55.7 (49-month high), but the employment sub-index fell to a six-year low.
Services PMI edged up to 51.3, with business inventory purchases hitting the second-highest level on record.
Market Impact : The data reflects economic resilience alongside emerging employment pressures, reinforcing the Fed’s dual focus on inflation and the labor market, which may influence future policy path expectations.
International Commodities Hormuz Strait Reopens, Middle East Crude Supply Flows Back
Following the reopening of the strait, Middle East crude has accelerated into European markets, pushing North Sea Brent benchmark components to two-year lows.
Oversupply concerns have intensified amid increased Atlantic basin supply.
Market Impact : Oil prices remain under pressure, highlighting the direct impact of geopolitical easing on energy supply and demand. Short-term bearish for crude but helps ease inflationary pressures.
Macroeconomic Policy South Korea Tax Reform Discussions Trigger Stock Market Crash; Storage Chip Rumors Worsen Sell-off
Multiple South Korean parties discussed including unrealized stock gains in comprehensive taxation, triggering a KOSPI circuit breaker, with Samsung and SK Hynix leading the decline.
Korean media reported that SK Hynix is slowing HBM4 production expansion and shifting resources to standard DRAM , citing reduced expectations for Nvidia ’s Rubin platform.
Market Impact : Policy uncertainty combined with supply chain rumors has weighed on global storage and semiconductor sectors, underscoring how regional policy can transmit effects to global tech supply chains.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance
Spot Gold : ~$4,090/oz, -0.34%
Spot Silver : ~$61/oz, -0.33%
WTI Crude: ~$72.5/barrel, -0.79%
Brent Crude: ~$76.4/barrel, -0.87%
US Dollar Index (DXY): 101.427, +0.05%
Driver Analysis : The reopening of the Hormuz Strait and resumption of Middle East crude shipments have intensified supply concerns in Europe, pushing North Sea benchmarks lower. Oil prices are under broad pressure. The dollar index remains elevated amid potential hawkish Fed signals and employment data, suppressing precious metals. Gold and silver softened under dollar strength and fluctuating risk sentiment, though geopolitical easing reduced some safe-haven demand. Institutions believe short-term supply-demand imbalances and macro policy expectations will continue to drive correlations. Lower oil prices may further ease global inflation pressures, while precious metals lack strong upward momentum in the near term.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : ~$62,866, -2.17%
ETH : ~$1,667, -3.8%
Total Crypto Market Cap: ~$2.24 trillion, -1.9%
Market Liquidations: 24h total ~$559 million (longs: $493 million)
Bitget BTC/ USDT Liquidation Heatmap: Current BTC price ~$62,765. Heavy long liquidation clusters sit below in the $61,500–$62,500 zone. A further pullback could trigger concentrated long stops and amplify downside. Above, the $63,500–$65,000 zone holds strong short liquidation pressure, with the densest cluster near $63,500 — a breakout could trigger a short squeeze and push BTC higher.
Spot ETF Net Flow: BTC spot ETFs saw a net outflow of $68.3 million yesterday.
Driver Analysis : The sell-off in US tech stocks spilled over into crypto, with storage chip rumors heightening risk aversion. BTC and ETH both came under pressure, though BTC showed relative resilience. Liquidations were dominated by longs, indicating high-leverage positions are being tested. ETFs still saw modest net inflows, showing institutional support at current levels. Macro-wise, dollar strength and geopolitical easing are acting in tandem. Technically, key supports are being tested. Institutions generally see heightened short-term volatility but believe the long-term inflow trend remains intact. Focus remains on ETF flows and macro data guidance for risk assets.
US Stock Indices Performance
Dow Jones: Closed ~51,667 (-0.09%)
S&P 500: Closed ~7,365 (-1.44%)
Nasdaq : Closed ~25,587 (-2.21%)
Tech Giants Performance
NVDA : $200.04 (-4.13%)
AAPL : $294.30 (-0.91%)
MSFT : $373.94 (+1.80%)
GOOGL : $346.13 (-0.98%)
AMZN : $234.11 (+0.57%)
META : $562.20 (-0.29%)
TSLA : $381.61 (-5.79%)
Summary & Driver Analysis : Tech giants were broadly under pressure, with Nasdaq posting a notable decline, mainly due to storage chip rumors and a broad semiconductor sell-off (Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell sharply). Google’s addition to the Dow is largely a symbolic adjustment. Individual stock performance diverged: TSLA found some support from specific news, while NVDA and GOOGL were dragged by supply chain concerns. The long-term AI demand thesis remains intact, but short-term high valuations and rumors amplified volatility. The market is watching catalysts such as Micron’s earnings.
[...]
Top Holdings by Open Interest (in $100 million units) : SPCX : 6.75 MU : 4.51 SKHX: 3.96 SNDK : 2.89 NVDA: 2.20 INTC : 1.67 MRVL : 1.47 GOOGL: 1.09 CRCL : 1.02 MSFT: 0.97 MSTR : 0.86 TSLA: 0.81 BZ : 0.65
[...]
Fund Flow : Increased positioning seen in SPCX, GOOGL, MSFT, NBIS , etc. Reduced positioning or outflows in MU, SKHX, SNDK, NVDA, INTC, MRVL, CRCL, MSTR, etc.
[...]
Representative stocks: Micron (MU) and SanDisk ( WDC ) fell over 13%, SK Hynix-related ADRs led the decline. ARM , Qualcomm , Western Digital, Applied Materials, and others dropped 7-10%+. Nvidia (NVDA) fell ~4%, AMD dropped over 5%.
[...]
Drivers : Multiple negative factors amplified market concerns. First, a joint proposal by South Korean lawmakers to include unrealized stock gains in the comprehensive tax system triggered a KOSPI circuit breaker, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix suffering heavy losses. Second, Korean media reported that SK Hynix is slowing HBM4 mass production expansion and redirecting resources to standard DRAM due to downward revisions in Nvidia’s next-generation Rubin platform production forecasts. This “small article” was quickly picked up by international outlets such as Bloomberg and CNBC, focusing trader attention on uncertainty in AI high-end storage demand.
[...]
In-depth Analysis : HBM has been viewed as a core bottleneck resource for AI training and inference, with the market previously expecting tight supply to support high growth and margin expansion for storage giants. The signal of slower capacity expansion, combined with adjustments in Nvidia demand guidance, has sparked widespread questions about whether the 2026 H2 AI capex peak might arrive earlier or moderate. This supply chain transmission effect has not only hit the storage sector but also spilled over to the broader semiconductor ecosystem, leading to concentrated profit-taking in high-valuation AI hardware stocks. In the short term, sector valuations are clearly under pressure. In the medium term, if Micron’s upcoming earnings provide positive guidance (e.g., higher HBM market share or healthy inventory), it could ease some pessimism. However, geopolitical policy uncertainty and the macro interest rate environment will still constrain rebound strength. Investors should closely track actual supply chain shipment data and major clients’ capex plans to distinguish cyclical fluctuations from structural opportunities.
[...]
Investment Implications : Short-term market reaction may be muted. Focus on fund flows and sector sentiment. Over the longer term, it should enhance Alphabet’s appeal among traditional investors and strengthen the position of tech weights in blue-chip portfolios. Investors are advised to track valuation expansion potential alongside growth in AI search and cloud businesses.
[...]
Other highlights: Nvidia (NVDA) shareholder meeting (9:00 AM PT, focusing on Blackwell and Vera architecture capacity ramp-up and AI infrastructure outlook).
